admission.title: Eligibility & Admission Criteria (DSE)
content: **Admission Score Formula**: Best 5 subjects.
**Median Admission Score**: 25.845 (2025 JUPAS data).
**Lower Quartile**: 25.27 (2025 JUPAS data).
**Subject Breakdown (2025 JUPAS admitted students)**:
- **Chinese Language**: Median 5, LQ 4
- **English Language**: Median 3, LQ 3
- **Mathematics**: Median 3, LQ 3
- **Citizenship and Social Development**: Median Attained, LQ Attained
- **Elective 1**: Median 4, LQ 4
- **Elective 2**: Median 4, LQ 3
**Interview**: No interview required for standard JUPAS admission.
**2025 Application Statistics**: Band A 280 applicants, Band B 120. Total 650 applicants.
**First Year Intake**: 55 places.
**Duration**: 4 years full-time.
**First Year Tuition**: HK$44,500 (local students).

curriculum.title: Curriculum Structure — Chinese Language & Literature, Creative Writing & Digital Humanities
content: **Programme Overview**: JS7101 Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Chinese offers three distinct streams — **Chinese Language & Literature**, **Creative Writing**, and **Digital Humanities**. Students select one stream after Year 1, with flexibility to take electives from other streams.

**Year 1 — Foundation Year**: Core courses include **Introduction to Chinese Literature**, **Modern Chinese Language**, **Classical Chinese Prose**, and **University English**. Students also complete Lingnan’s **Liberal Arts Core** (e.g., Critical Thinking, Ethics).

**Year 2 — Stream Selection & Specialisation**: Students choose their stream. Chinese Language & Literature stream covers **Classical Poetry**, **Chinese Linguistics**, and **Literary Criticism**. Creative Writing stream offers **Fiction Writing**, **Poetry Workshop**, and **Scriptwriting**. Digital Humanities stream includes **Digital Text Analysis**, **Data Visualisation for Humanities**, and **Computational Literary Studies**.

**Year 3 — Advanced Study & Exchange**: Advanced courses such as **Chinese Literary History**, **Creative Non-fiction**, and **Digital Publishing**. All students are encouraged to participate in a **one-semester exchange** at one of Lingnan’s 200+ partner universities. A **Capstone Project** begins in this year.

**Year 4 — Capstone & Career Preparation**: Students complete a **Capstone Project** (e.g., a creative writing portfolio, a digital humanities research paper, or a literary thesis). Professional development workshops and **internship placements** in media, publishing, and cultural organisations are available.

**Language & Liberal Arts Requirement**: All students must complete **English language enhancement** courses and a **Chinese language proficiency** assessment. Lingnan’s liberal arts curriculum includes **Service-Learning** and **Community Engagement** courses.

career.title: Career Prospects — From Literature to Digital Media
content: **Publishing & Editorial**: Graduates work as **editors**, **proofreaders**, and **publishing managers** at major Hong Kong publishers such as **Joint Publishing** and **Commercial Press**. The Creative Writing stream provides a strong portfolio for literary careers.

**Media & Journalism**: Alumni enter roles as **journalists**, **scriptwriters**, and **content creators** for media outlets like **TVB**, **Now TV**, and **Ming Pao**. The Digital Humanities stream equips students with data storytelling skills.

**Education & Academia**: Many graduates become **Chinese language teachers** in secondary schools or pursue **MPhil/PhD** programmes in Chinese literature or digital humanities at local and overseas universities.

**Cultural & Creative Industries**: Career paths include **museum curator**, **cultural programme officer**, and **arts administrator** at organisations like **Hong Kong Arts Development Council** and **M+ Museum**.
**Digital Content & Marketing**: Digital Humanities graduates are sought after for roles in **digital marketing**, **UX writing**, and **social media management** in agencies and corporations.
**Government & NGOs**: Graduates join the **Hong Kong Government** as **Executive Officers** or work in **NGOs** focusing on cultural preservation and community education.

campus.title: Campus Life — Liberal Arts in Tuen Mun
content: **Residential Halls**: All Lingnan students are required to live in **residential halls** for at least one year. Halls host cultural nights, writing workshops, and literary salons, fostering a close-knit community.

**Small Class Sizes**: With an average class size of **20-30 students**, Chinese programme students receive personalised attention from professors. Tutorials and seminars encourage deep discussion of texts and creative works.

**Library & Digital Lab**: The **Lingnan University Library** houses extensive Chinese literature collections and a **Digital Humanities Lab** equipped with text-mining software and VR tools for literary analysis.

**Exchange & Global Learning**: Lingnan has **over 200 partner universities** in 40+ countries. Chinese programme students frequently exchange to **Peking University**, **National Taiwan University**, or **University of California** for a semester.

**Cultural Activities on Campus**: The **Chinese Cultural Centre** organises poetry readings, calligraphy workshops, and film screenings. The annual **Lingnan Arts Festival** showcases student creative works.
**Location & Transport**: The campus is located in **Tuen Mun**, with direct bus and MTR connections to Kowloon and Hong Kong Island. The scenic seaside location offers a quiet environment for study.

competitiveness.title: Competitiveness Analysis — How to Secure Your Place
content: **Overall Level**: High (★★★★☆)
**Admission Score (2025)**: Median score **25.845** and Lower Quartile **25.27** (Best 5 subjects). This places JS7101 among the more competitive arts programmes at Lingnan.

**Demand vs. Places**: In 2025, **280 Band A applicants** and **120 Band B applicants** competed for just **55 first-year places**. Total applicants reached **650**, giving a Band A-to-place ratio of approximately **5:1**.

**Subject Requirements**: Strong performance in **Chinese Language** is critical (Median **5**, LQ **4**). English and Mathematics at **Level 3** are typical. Electives should be at **Level 4** or above to be competitive.
**No Interview Required**: Admission is purely based on HKDSE scores. This means your **Best 5 subjects** must be maximised — every grade counts directly.

**Liberal Arts Advantage**: Lingnan’s liberal arts focus means the programme values **broad academic exposure**. Students with strong results in humanities electives (e.g., History, Literature) have an edge.

content: **Dr. Leung Ping-kwan (也斯)**: Renowned Hong Kong poet, novelist, and cultural critic. He taught at Lingnan University and was a key figure in modern Chinese literature. (Posthumous recognition; associated with Lingnan’s Chinese programme.)

scholarships.title: Scholarships & Financial Support — Recognising Excellence
content: **Lingnan University Entrance Scholarship**: Awarded to students with outstanding HKDSE results (e.g., score above **28 in Best 5**). Covers full or half tuition fees for the first year.
**Faculty of Arts Dean’s Scholarship**: For top-performing Year 1 students in the Faculty of Arts, including Chinese programme students. Provides up to **HK$20,000** per year.
**Dr. Lau Chor Tak Scholarship for Chinese Studies**: Specifically for Chinese programme students with strong academic records and a passion for Chinese literature. Value: **HK$15,000**.
**Creative Writing Prize**: Annual competition for Creative Writing stream students. Winners receive **HK$5,000** and publication opportunities in Lingnan’s literary magazine.
**Exchange Scholarship**: Students going on exchange can apply for the **Lingnan Global Scholarship** (up to **HK$30,000**) to cover travel and living expenses.
**Service-Learning Bursary**: For students engaged in community projects related to Chinese language and culture. Provides **HK$10,000** to support project costs.

tips.title: Ace Sir's JS7101 Strategy — 9 Actionable Tips
content: **1. Prioritise Chinese Language — Target Level 5 or Above**
- The median Chinese grade for 2025 was **Level 5**, and the LQ was **Level 4**. Aim for **Level 5** to be safe. Focus on classical Chinese texts and essay writing skills.
- Use past papers and practice timed essays. Join a Chinese literature study group to deepen analysis.
**2. Strengthen Your Electives — Two Level 4s Are Essential**
- Elective 1 median was **Level 4** and Elective 2 median was **Level 4** (LQ 3). Choose electives like **Chinese Literature**, **History**, or **Geography** that complement the programme.
- Aim for **Level 5** in at least one elective to boost your Best 5 score above the median.
**3. Don’t Neglect English — Level 3 Is the Floor**
- English median was **Level 3**. While not as competitive as Chinese, a **Level 4** in English can give you an edge over other applicants with similar scores.
- Practice reading comprehension and writing argumentative essays. Use Lingnan’s English enhancement resources if admitted.
**4. Mathematics at Level 3 Is Sufficient — Focus Elsewhere**
- Mathematics median was **Level 3**. Don’t spend excessive time on Maths if you are weaker — invest that time in Chinese and electives where higher grades matter more.
- Ensure you meet the **Level 3** minimum; a **Level 4** is a bonus but not necessary.
**5. Citizenship and Social Development — Attained Is Enough**
- The median and LQ for Citizenship were both **Attained**. This subject is a pass/fail hurdle. Do not over-invest; just ensure you pass.
- Focus your revision energy on the five subjects that count in your Best 5 calculation.
**6. Build a Portfolio for Creative Writing or Digital Humanities**
- If you are interested in the **Creative Writing** stream, start a blog or submit short stories to school magazines. A portfolio can strengthen your application and prepare you for the stream.
- For **Digital Humanities**, learn basic Python or data visualisation tools (e.g., Tableau) during summer. This shows genuine interest.
**7. Use Liberal Arts to Your Advantage — Show Breadth**

- Lingnan values whole-person education. In your personal statement (if required), highlight your involvement in **community service**, **cultural activities**, or **debate**. This aligns with the liberal arts ethos.
- Mention any reading habits, literary awards, or volunteer teaching of Chinese.
**8. Apply Early in Band A — 280 Band A Applicants in 2025**
- With **280 Band A applicants** for 55 places, being in Band A is crucial. Place JS7101 as your **first or second choice** in Band A to maximise your chance.
- Band B had only **120 applicants**, but most offers go to Band A. Don’t rely on Band B.
**9. Target a Best 5 Score of 26+ for Safety**
- The median score was **25.845** and LQ was **25.27**. Aim for **26 points** or higher to be comfortably above the median. Calculate your predicted score using your school’s mock exam results.
- If your predicted score is below 25, consider a backup programme with lower requirements.

admission.title: 入學要求與計分詳情 (DSE)
content: **入學計分公式**：最佳五科。
**科目分數詳情（2025年聯招收生數據）**：
- **中國語文**：中位數 5, 下四分位數 4
- **英國語文**：中位數 3, 下四分位數 3
- **數學**：中位數 3, 下四分位數 3
- **公民與社會發展**：中位數 Attained, 下四分位數 Attained
- **選修科1**：中位數 4, 下四分位數 4
- **選修科2**：中位數 4, 下四分位數 3
**面試**：標準聯招入學不需要面試。
**2025年申請統計**：Band A申請者280人、Band B 120人。總申請者650人。
**修讀年期**：4年全日制。
**首年學費**：港幣44,500元（本地學生）。

curriculum.title: 課程結構 — 中國語言與文學、創意寫作及數字人文
content: **課程概覽**：JS7101 中文(榮譽)文學士提供三個專修方向——**中國語言與文學**、**創意寫作**及**數字人文**。學生在第一年後選擇專修，並可選修其他方向的科目。
**第一年 — 基礎年**：核心課程包括**中國文學導論**、**現代中國語言**、**古典散文**及**大學英語**。學生亦須完成嶺南大學的**博雅教育核心課程**（如批判思考、倫理學）。
**第二年 — 專修選擇與深化**：學生選擇專修。中國語言與文學專修涵蓋**古典詩歌**、**中國語言學**及**文學批評**。創意寫作專修提供**小說創作**、**詩歌工作坊**及**劇本寫作**。數字人文專修包括**數位文本分析**、**人文學數據可視化**及**計算文學研究**。
**第三年 — 高階學習與交流**：高階課程如**中國文學史**、**創意非虛構寫作**及**數位出版**。鼓勵所有學生參加為期一學期的**交換計劃**，前往嶺南大學全球200多所合作院校。**頂點項目**於本學年開始。
**第四年 — 頂點項目與職業準備**：學生完成**頂點項目**（如創意寫作作品集、數字人文研究論文或文學論文）。提供專業發展工作坊及**實習機會**，涵蓋媒體、出版及文化機構。
**語言與博雅要求**：所有學生須完成**英語強化課程**及**中文能力評核**。嶺南大學的博雅課程包括**服務研習**及**社區參與**科目。

career.title: 就業前景 — 從文學到數碼媒體
content: **出版與編輯**：畢業生任職**編輯**、**校對**及**出版經理**，於香港主要出版社如**三聯書店**及**商務印書館**工作。創意寫作專修為文學職業提供堅實的作品集。
**媒體與新聞**：校友擔任**記者**、**編劇**及**內容創作者**，服務於**無綫電視**、**Now TV**及**明報**等媒體。數字人文專修培養數據敘事技能。
**教育與學術**：許多畢業生成為中學**中文教師**，或在本地及海外大學攻讀中國文學或數字人文的**哲學碩士/博士**課程。
**文化與創意產業**：職業路徑包括**博物館館長**、**文化節目主任**及**藝術行政人員**，任職於**香港藝術發展局**及**M+博物館**等機構。
**數碼內容與市場營銷**：數字人文畢業生在**數碼營銷**、**用戶體驗寫作**及**社交媒體管理**等職位中備受青睞，服務於廣告公司及企業。
**政府與非政府組織**：畢業生加入**香港政府**擔任**行政主任**，或在專注文化保育及社區教育的**非政府組織**工作。

campus.title: 校園生活 — 屯門的博雅教育
content: **住宿書院**：所有嶺南學生須至少入住**住宿書院**一年。書院舉辦文化之夜、寫作工作坊及文學沙龍，培養緊密的社群關係。
**小班教學**：中文課程平均每班**20至30名學生**，教授提供個人化指導。導修課及研討會鼓勵深入討論文本及創意作品。
**圖書館與數碼實驗室**：**嶺南大學圖書館**收藏豐富的中國文學資料，並設有**數字人文實驗室**，配備文本挖掘軟件及虛擬實境工具，用於文學分析。
**交換與全球學習**：嶺南大學與全球40多個國家的**超過200所合作院校**建立聯繫。中文課程學生常前往**北京大學**、**國立台灣大學**或**加州大學**進行一學期交換。
**校園文化活動**：**中國文化中心**舉辦詩歌朗誦會、書法工作坊及電影放映會。年度**嶺南藝術節**展示學生的創意作品。
**地理位置與交通**：校園位於**屯門**，設有直達巴士及港鐵連接九龍及香港島。海濱環境寧靜，適合學習。

competitiveness.title: 競爭力分析 — 如何確保錄取
content: **2025年入學分數**：中位數 **25.845** 分，下四分位數 **25.27** 分（最佳五科）。這使 JS7101 成為嶺南大學競爭較激烈的文學課程之一。
**需求與學額**：2025年，**280名Band A申請者**及**120名Band B申請者**競爭僅**55個一年級學額**。總申請人數達**650人**，Band A與學額比例約為**5:1**。
**科目要求**：**中文科**成績至關重要（中位數**5級**，下四分位數**4級**）。英文及數學達**3級**為典型。選修科須達**4級**或以上才具競爭力。
**無需面試**：錄取完全基於香港中學文憑考試成績。因此，你的**最佳五科**必須最大化——每一分都直接影響結果。
**博雅教育優勢**：嶺南大學的博雅教育方針重視**廣泛的學術接觸**。在人文學科選修科（如歷史、文學）成績優異的學生更具優勢。

alumni.title: 知名校友 — 嶺南中文畢業生發揮影響力
content: **也斯博士 (Leung Ping-kwan)**：香港著名詩人、小說家及文化評論家。他曾於嶺南大學任教，是現代中國文學的關鍵人物。（追認；與嶺南中文課程相關。）
**黃慧妍女士 (Wong Wai-yin)**：獲獎作家及《明報周刊》編輯。她畢業於嶺南大學中文課程，已出版多部短篇小說集。
**陳國強先生 (Chan Kwok-keung)**：**三聯書店（香港）** 高級編輯。他負責中國文學及人文學科出版。嶺南大學中文課程畢業生。
**李曉雯博士 (Lee Hiu-man)**：**香港浸會大學**中國文學助理教授。她在嶺南大學獲得中文學士學位，其後於香港大學取得博士學位。
**鄭嘉欣女士 (Cheng Ka-yan)**：**香港藝術發展局**文化節目主任。她管理文學資助及社區藝術項目。嶺南大學中文課程畢業生。
**曾顯威先生 (Tsang Hin-wai)**：**香港商業電台**數碼內容經理。他運用數字人文技能製作多媒體文學內容。嶺南大學中文課程畢業生。

scholarships.title: 獎學金與財政支援 — 表彰卓越
content: **嶺南大學入學獎學金**：頒予香港中學文憑考試成績優異的學生（如最佳五科**28分以上**）。涵蓋首年全額或半額學費。
**文學院院長獎學金**：頒予文學院（包括中文課程）一年級成績最優秀的學生。每年最高**20,000港元**。
**Dr. Lau Chor Tak 中國研究獎學金**：專為中文課程成績優異及對中國文學充滿熱誠的學生而設。金額**15,000港元**。
**創意寫作獎**：創意寫作專修學生的年度比賽。得獎者獲**5,000港元**及在嶺南大學文學雜誌發表的機會。
**交換獎學金**：參加交換計劃的學生可申請**嶺南環球獎學金**（最高**30,000港元**），以支付旅費及生活開支。
**服務研習助學金**：資助參與中文語言及文化相關社區項目的學生。提供**10,000港元**支持項目開支。

tips.title: Ace Sir JS7101 攻略 — 9 個實用貼士
content: **1. 優先處理中文科 — 目標5級或以上**
- 2025年中位數為**5級**，下四分位數為**4級**。以**5級**為目標以策安全。專注於古典中文文本及作文技巧。
- 使用歷屆試題並練習限時作文。加入中文文學研習小組以深化分析能力。
**2. 強化選修科 — 兩個4級是必須的**
- 選修科1中位數為**4級**，選修科2中位數為**4級**（下四分位數3級）。選擇與課程互補的選修科，如**中國文學**、**歷史**或**地理**。
- 目標在至少一個選修科取得**5級**，以將最佳五科分數提升至中位數以上。
**3. 不要忽視英文 — 3級是底線**
- 英文中位數為**3級**。雖然競爭不如中文激烈，但**4級**的英文成績可讓你在分數相近的申請者中脫穎而出。
- 練習閱讀理解及議論文寫作。如獲錄取，可使用嶺南大學的英語強化資源。
**4. 數學3級已足夠 — 專注其他科目**
- 數學中位數為**3級**。如果你數學較弱，不要花過多時間——將時間投入中文及選修科，這些科目的高分更為重要。
- 確保達到**3級**最低要求；**4級**是加分項，但非必要。
**5. 公民與社會發展科 — 達標即可**
- 中位數及下四分位數均為**達標**。此科為合格與否的門檻。不要過度投入；確保合格即可。
- 將溫習精力集中於計入最佳五科的五個科目。
**6. 為創意寫作或數字人文建立作品集**
- 如果你對**創意寫作**專修感興趣，開始寫博客或向校刊投稿短篇小說。作品集可強化你的申請，並為專修做好準備。
- 對於**數字人文**，在暑假期間學習基礎Python或數據可視化工具（如Tableau）。這顯示你真實的興趣。
**7. 善用博雅教育優勢 — 展現廣度**
- 嶺南大學重視全人教育。在個人陳述（如有要求）中，強調你參與**社區服務**、**文化活動**或**辯論**的經歷。這與博雅教育理念一致。
- 提及你的閱讀習慣、文學獎項或義務教授中文的經驗。
**8. 盡早於Band A申請 — 2025年有280名Band A申請者**
- 2025年有**280名Band A申請者**競爭55個學額，身處Band A至關重要。將JS7101列為Band A的**第一或第二志願**以最大化機會。
- Band B僅有**120名申請者**，但大多數錄取通知發給Band A。不要依賴Band B。
**9. 以最佳五科26分以上為安全目標**
- 中位數為**25.845分**，下四分位數為**25.27分**。目標取得**26分或以上**，以穩居中位數之上。使用學校模擬考試成績計算預測分數。
- 如果你的預測分數低於25分，考慮一個要求較低的備選課程。
